Critical Flaw in Pillow Allows Code Execution #759 – NOVEMBER 3, 2026
VIEW IN BROWSER



Critical Flaw in Pillow Allows Code Execution
A critical flaw was found in Pillow, the popular image library. A specially crafted EPS file could result in code execution. Pillow 13.0.0 fixed this and several other issues. This post describes the release and exploit.
SWATI KHANDELWAI

Python’s Experimental JIT to Be Removed
PEP 836 has been withdrawn and the experimental JIT is to be removed from CPython’s main branch. This article talks about the JIT’s journey and what still may be in store.
JOE BROCKMEIER

CodeAF: 78% on DeepSWE with an Open Model
With DeepSeek V4.1 Flash, CodeAF fixed 88 of 113 GitHub issues on DeepSWE. Against Codex and eight other harnesses on one open model, it ranked #1 at the lowest cost per fix. CodeAF is an open-source coding harness built for open models, and works with closed models too. Star on GitHub

Move Past the Chat Window With Codex CLI
If you’re still pasting code and tracebacks into a chat, let an agent work inside your project instead. Codex CLI runs in your terminal, reads your files, runs your tests, and follows the project rules you write in an AGENTS.md file. Over two live days on November 14–15, you’ll build a full Python CLI app this way, from an empty directory to GitHub.

Google Adopts Pyrefly for Typechecking
Python is one of the primary languages at Google, powering everything from machine learning research to developer infrastructure and data pipelines. Replacing previous type-checking infrastructure with Pyrefly provided significant speedups for engineers and agents alike, while substantially reducing build-system compute resources.

Polars 2.0: Streaming by Default and Stricter Types
Polars 2.0 makes lazy queries faster without code changes, but its new defaults can affect existing workflows. This article compares Polars 1.x and 2.0, covering streaming performance, spill-to-disk, changes to join ordering, and stricter type checking that catches silent precision loss.

Django as a Simple Static Site Builder
Combining three libraries: nanodjango, django-nanopages, and django-distill, you can create a static site generator in just a few lines of code. Why learn another tool when you already know Django?

PyPI Now Limits Versions to 128 Characters
Across roughly 10 million releases, only two have version strings longer than 128 characters, so this change doesn’t really effect anyone. The new limit is mostly to keep page rendering for projects to be reasonable and the rule is only for PyPI and won’t be enforced by tools such as pip or uv.

OpenTeams’ PyTorch team reviews their 2026 contributions, in a year when PyTorch received 58% more pull requests than the same period of 2025, a growing share of them written with AI coding agents. Highlights include a redesign of the symbolic interpreter in torch.compile, day 1 compiler support for Python 3.15, a new operator, and a build backend re-write!

Bayesian Optimization for Efficient Hyperparameter Search
Instead of testing every hyperparameter combination, Bayesian optimization uses results from earlier trials to decide what to try next. This hands-on tutorial builds it step by step with scikit-learn’s GaussianProcessRegressor and a custom Expected Improvement function, plotting the model’s predictions and uncertainty along with each point the search picks.

Pendulum and the Most Cursed + Operator in All of Python
Pendulum, a popular Python datetime library, has a + operator that inspects the call stack to decide which answer to give you. The post explains how it ended up there, and why the design behind it, a “drop-in” subclass of datetime, still matters for your code now that the hack itself has been patched.
ARIE BOVENBERG • Shared by Arie Bovenberg

Checking Email Reputation, and Allowing Outlook Again
Two years ago, PyPI prohibited Outlook email domains in the registration of new accounts due to a large malware campaign. With an update to how email reputation is calculated, addresses from outlook.com and hotmail.com can once more be used.
